0.0.n: This is the name of the person being addressed.

0.1.n: Added after Gen’s name to show affection or familiarity.

0.3.n: Read as なに here, asking which food the listener wants.

0.4.n: With 食べたい, が marks the thing someone wants to eat.

0.5.n: 食べる changes to 食べたい with たい to express desire; rising intonation makes this a casual question.

1.0.n: A brief reaction showing surprise or asking the speaker to repeat something.

2.0.n: Read as なに here, asking which food the listener wants.

2.1.n: With 食べたい, が marks the thing someone wants to eat.

2.2.n: 食べる changes to 食べたい with たい to express desire; rising intonation makes this a casual question.

3.0.n: 韓国 usually refers to South Korea; here it identifies the cuisine.

3.1.n: Links 韓国 to デリバリー, describing the delivery food as Korean.

3.2.n: An English loanword used here for food ordered for delivery.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out you when it is clear who is being asked.

1.tip: Said with rising intonation, え？ can ask someone to repeat what they said.

2.tip: The たい ending expresses wanting to do something.

3.tip: This short answer means Korean food for delivery, not a delivery arriving from Korea.
